# HashiCorp Raft Divergences

In 2013 HashiCorp created its own Raft implementation based on the just
released [Raft paper by Diego Ongaro and John Ousterhout][paper]. This was
before [Diego's subsequent Raft dissertation][diss] in 2014, and long before
third party analyses such as Heidi Howard and Ittai Abraham's [Raft does not
Guarantee Liveness in the face of Network Faults ][live]
in 2020.[^1]

HashiCorp's Raft library usage grew rapidly through its use in [Consul][consul]
and [Nomad][nomad], and [later Vault][vault], in parallel with rapidly
expanding use in [etcd][etcd] and other implementations.

The explosion in activity between live systems and research led to a wide
divergence between not only implementations, but implementations and the
original paper and dissertation.

This document attempts to explain where HashiCorp Raft either meaningfully diverges
from the original Raft paper, or makes an implementation choice not explicitly
outlined in the paper.

This is **not** expected to be a comprehensive list. Additions and edits are
welcome!

## Asynchronous Heartbeats

The Raft paper defines heartbeats as empty AppendEntries RPCs which are sent by
the leader to each server after elections and during idle periods to prevent
election timeouts.

HashiCorp Raft performs [heartbeating concurrently][async-heart] with other
AppendEntries RPCs to avoid having to set the election timeout high enough to
account for the max acceptable disk operation. This allows the heartbeat
timeout to detect network partitions much more quickly without risking causing
an election during periodic but ephemeral spikes in disk io latency.

## Rejecting votes when there's already a leader

The [Raft does not Guarantee liveness][live] paper describes how certain
partitions can prevent Raft clusters from making progress by causing continual
elections.

HashiCorp Raft implements the second of the suggested fixes from Howard's
paper: rejecting vote request RPCs when there is already an established leader.
The paper defines this more precisely as:

> ...ignore RequestVote RPCs if they have received an AppendEntries RPC from
> the leader within the election timeout. 

This approach is actually mentioned in the Cluster membership changes section
of the original Raft paper, but explicitly excludes its use during "normal"
elections:

> To prevent this problem, servers disregard RequestVote RPCs when they believe
> a current leader exists. Specifically, if a server receives a RequestVote RPC
> within the minimum election timeout of hearing from a current leader, it does
> not update its term or grant its vote.  This does not affect normal
> elections...

So HashiCorp Raft follows the later paper's suggestion and ignores the original
paper's exclusion of this logic during normal operation.

## Pre-Vote

[HashiCorp Raft implements the Pre-Vote extension][prevote-pr] defined in the
[Raft dissertation][diss] (§9.6). Pre-Vote is an optimization where a candidate
discovers whether its index is up to date and therefore able to win an election
before incrementing its term and causing an election.

The Pre-Vote extension is enabled by default but may be disabled in using the
[Config.PreVoteDisabled][prevote-config] flag.

## Leadership Transfer

[HashiCorp Raft implements the Leadership Transfer extension][transleader-pr]
as defined in the [Raft dissertation][diss] (§3.10). Leadership transfer is an
optimization that allows the current leader to hand off leadership to a
follower to avoid waiting for the election timeout during regular operations
such as restarts and upgrades.

While leadership transfer in defined in the Raft dissertation, HashiCorp Raft
extends the specification slightly because of _another_ divergence in HashiCorp
Raft: [rejecting votes when there's already a
leader](#rejecting-votes-when-theres-already-a-leader). Since other followers
would reject the intended new-leader's request for a vote, HashiCorp Raft adds
an extra [`LeadershipTransfer` flag][transleader-flag] to override that
behavior in the case of leadership transfers.

All Raft members should support leadership transfers before a transfer is
attempted. The feature is **not** enabled by default and requires explicitly
triggering at the application level. Consul was the first to implement this via
mechanisms in their [API/CLI][transleader-cli] and [graceful agent
shutdown][transleader-shutdown].

item.text: Two concrete failure modes are visible in the startup path: recovery advances `lastApplied` before the configuration scan, which appears to skip every committed configuration entry; and recovery synchronously fills an FSM channel before the FSM goroutine starts, which can deadlock for enough logs. I’m converting both into isolated regression tests now.

# UNRELEASED

IMPROVEMENETS

* Added a flag to skip legacy duplicate telemetry. [GH-630](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/630)

# 1.7.0 (June 5th, 2024)

CHANGES

* Raft multi version testing [GH-559](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/559)

IMPROVEMENTS

* Raft pre-vote extension implementation, activated by default. [GH-530](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/530)

BUG FIXES

* Fix serialize NetworkTransport data race on ServerAddr(). [GH-591](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/591)

# 1.6.1 (January 8th, 2024)

CHANGES

* Add reference use of Hashicorp Raft. [GH-584](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/584)
* [COMPLIANCE] Add Copyright and License Headers. [GH-580](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/580)

IMPROVEMENTS

* Bump github.com/hashicorp/go-hclog from 1.5.0 to 1.6.2. [GH-583](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/583)

BUG FIXES

* Fix rare leadership transfer failures when writes happen during transfer. [GH-581](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/581)

# 1.6.0 (November 15th, 2023)

CHANGES

* Upgrade hashicorp/go-msgpack to v2, with go.mod upgraded from v0.5.5 to v2.1.1. [GH-577](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/577)

  go-msgpack v2.1.1 is by default binary compatible with v0.5.5 ("non-builtin" encoding of `time.Time`), but can decode messages produced by v1.1.5 as well ("builtin" encoding of `time.Time`).

  However, if users of this library overrode the version of go-msgpack (especially to v1), this **could break** compatibility if raft nodes are running a mix of versions.

  This compatibility can be configured at runtime in Raft using `NetworkTransportConfig.MsgpackUseNewTimeFormat` -- the default is `false`, which maintains compatibility with `go-msgpack` v0.5.5, but if set to `true`, will be compatible with `go-msgpack` v1.1.5.

IMPROVEMENTS

* Push to notify channel when shutting down. [GH-567](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/567)
* Add CommitIndex API [GH-560](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/560)
* Document some Apply error cases better [GH-561](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/561)

BUG FIXES

* Race with `candidateFromLeadershipTransfer` [GH-570](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/570)


# 1.5.0 (April 21st, 2023)

IMPROVEMENTS
* Fixed a performance anomaly related to pipelining RPCs that caused large increases in commit latency under high write throughput. Default behavior has changed. For more information see #541.

# 1.4.0 (March 17th, 2023)

FEATURES
* Support log stores with a monotonically increasing index.  Implementing a log store with the `MonotonicLogStore` interface where `IsMonotonic()` returns true will allow Raft to clear all previous logs on user restores of Raft snapshots.

BUG FIXES
* Restoring a snapshot with the raft-wal log store caused a panic due to index gap that is created during snapshot restores.

# 1.3.0 (April 22nd, 2021)

IMPROVEMENTS

* Added metrics for `oldestLogAge` and `lastRestoreDuration` to monitor capacity issues that can cause unrecoverable cluster failure  [[GH-452](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/452)][[GH-454](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/454/files)]
* Made `TrailingLogs`, `SnapshotInterval` and `SnapshotThreshold` reloadable at runtime using a new `ReloadConfig` method. This allows recovery from cases where there are not enough logs retained for followers to catchup after a restart. [[GH-444](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/444)]
* Inclusify the repository by switching to main [[GH-446](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/446)]
* Add option for a buffered `ApplyCh` if `MaxAppendEntries` is enabled [[GH-445](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/445)]
* Add string to `LogType` for more human readable debugging [[GH-442](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/442)]
* Extract fuzzy testing into its own module [[GH-459](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/459)]

BUG FIXES
* Update LogCache `StoreLogs()` to capture an error that would previously cause a panic [[GH-460](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/460)]

# 1.2.0 (October 5th, 2020)

IMPROVEMENTS

* Remove `StartAsLeader` configuration option [[GH-364](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/386)]
* Allow futures to react to `Shutdown()` to prevent a deadlock with `takeSnapshot()` [[GH-390](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/390)]
* Prevent non-voters from becoming eligible for leadership elections [[GH-398](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/398)]
* Remove an unneeded `io.Copy` from snapshot writes [[GH-399](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/399)]
* Log decoded candidate address in `duplicate requestVote` warning [[GH-400](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/400)]
* Prevent starting a TCP transport when IP address is `nil` [[GH-403](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/403)]
* Reject leadership transfer requests when in candidate state to prevent indefinite blocking while unable to elect a leader [[GH-413](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/413)]
* Add labels for metric metadata to reduce cardinality of metric names [[GH-409](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/409)]
* Add peers metric [[GH-413](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/431)]

BUG FIXES

* Make `LeaderCh` always deliver the latest leadership transition [[GH-384](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/384)]
* Handle updating an existing peer in `startStopReplication` [[GH-419](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/419)]

# 1.1.2 (January 17th, 2020)

FEATURES

* Improve FSM apply performance through batching. Implementing the `BatchingFSM` interface enables this new feature [[GH-364](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/364)]
* Add ability to obtain Raft configuration before Raft starts with GetConfiguration [[GH-369](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/369)]

IMPROVEMENTS

* Remove lint violations and add a `make` rule for running the linter.
* Replace logger with hclog [[GH-360](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/360)]
* Read latest configuration independently from main loop [[GH-379](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/379)]

BUG FIXES

* Export the leader field in LeaderObservation [[GH-357](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/357)]
* Fix snapshot to not attempt to truncate a negative range [[GH-358](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/358)]
* Check for shutdown in inmemPipeline before sending RPCs [[GH-276](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/276)]

# 1.1.1 (July 23rd, 2019)

FEATURES

* Add support for extensions to be sent on log entries [[GH-353](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/353)]
* Add config option to skip snapshot restore on startup [[GH-340](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/340)]
* Add optional configuration store interface [[GH-339](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/339)]

IMPROVEMENTS

* Break out of group commit early when no logs are present [[GH-341](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/341)]

BUGFIXES

* Fix 64-bit counters on 32-bit platforms [[GH-344](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/344)]
* Don't defer closing source in recover/restore operations since it's in a loop [[GH-337](https://github.com/hashicorp/raft/pull/337)]

# 1.1.0 (May 23rd, 2019)

# HashiCorp Raft correctness audit

Source identity: `0f543c056e7e577a54b819a62116335c9661a13a`

The implementation's new `RestoreCommittedLogs` startup mode has two independently
reproducible correctness defects. Both occur with supported configuration values
and do not require a cluster-wide fault.

## Finding 1: committed-log recovery discards the persisted cluster configuration

Severity: high

Affected code:

- `api.go:607-625`: `NewRaft` invokes `restoreFromCommittedLogs`, then starts its
  configuration scan at `max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1`.
- `api.go:720-755`: `restoreFromCommittedLogs` sets `lastApplied` to the persisted
  commit index via `processLogs`.
- `raft.go:1296-1363`: `processLogs` applies entries to the FSM, but never calls
  `processConfigurationLogEntry` or updates `r.configurations`.

Expected behavior: enabling `RestoreCommittedLogs` should replay the committed
log suffix to the FSM without losing Raft's own persistent state. In particular,
after restart, the latest committed configuration must be reconstructed from
configuration entries in that suffix. This is the behavior of the same startup
path with `RestoreCommittedLogs` disabled, and is required before the node can
evaluate elections or membership safely.

Actual behavior: on startup, `processLogs` advances `lastApplied` through the
persisted commit index. The subsequent configuration scan deliberately starts
after `lastApplied`, so it skips every configuration entry in the replayed
range. No other recovery step populates `r.configurations`. A restarted node can
therefore have an empty or stale `latest` configuration even though its log
contains the committed current configuration.

This occurs without a snapshot. With one bootstrapped voter and one committed
client command, the persisted tracker reaches the committed no-op and command.
After restart, the log still contains the bootstrap configuration at index 1,
but `restarted.GetConfiguration()` returns an empty configuration and the node
logs `initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]`.

Reproduction: `TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsRestoresConfiguration` in
`audit_repro_test.go`.

Command:

```text
go test -run '^TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsRestoresConfiguration$' -count=1 -v .
```

Observed result:

```text
server-...: initial configuration: index=1 servers="[{Suffrage:Voter ID:server-... Address:...}]"
server-...: initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]
audit_repro_test.go:50: configuration after recovery = [], want local server "server-..."
--- FAIL: TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsRestoresConfiguration (0.33s)
```

The first `initial configuration` line is the original startup. The second is
the recovery-enabled restart immediately after `NewRaft` returns.
Running this test ten times produced ten failures, so the observation is not a
startup race.

Alternative considered: perhaps the FSM-side configuration application is
intended to replace the Raft configuration scan. It cannot: `processLogs` only
queues `commitTuple`s for `runFSM`; `runFSM` may call an application
`ConfigurationStore`, but never mutates `Raft.configurations`, which is used by
elections, quorum calculation, and `GetConfiguration`.

## Finding 2: startup deadlocks while replaying enough committed batches

Severity: medium; deterministic availability failure during startup

Affected code:

- `api.go:607-628`: committed-log recovery completes before `runFSM` is started.
- `api.go:560`: `fsmMutateCh` has a fixed buffer of 128 items.
- `raft.go:1302-1317`: `processLogs` sends one batch per `MaxAppendEntries`
  entries and blocks when the channel is full.

Expected behavior: `NewRaft` should return after replaying any number of
persisted committed entries that fit the supported configuration. Writes to the
FSM mutation channel must have a live consumer or must not outnumber its buffer
before startup completes.

Actual behavior: `restoreFromCommittedLogs` calls `processLogs`, which must put
every batch on `fsmMutateCh`; however, `runFSM` is only started after recovery
returns. Consequently, more than 128 batches block `NewRaft` forever while it
waits for a consumer it has not yet launched.

With the supported `MaxAppendEntries = 1`, only 129 committed entries that
produce FSM batches are needed to trigger the deadlock. The reproducer commits
130 such entries, including the bootstrap configuration, and leaves one later
entry in storage. With larger legal batch sizes, the required committed log
count is correspondingly larger, but remains finite and can occur in normal
operation.

Reproduction: `TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsDoesNotDeadlockBeforeRunFSM` in
`audit_repro_test.go`.

Commands:

```text
go test -run '^TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsDoesNotDeadlockBeforeRunFSM$' -count=1 -v .
```

Observed result:

```text
audit_repro_test.go:107: NewRaft deadlocked while restoring 130 committed entries
--- FAIL: TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsDoesNotDeadlockBeforeRunFSM (2.00s)
```

Alternative considered: `BatchApplyCh` could relieve the problem if it allowed
`runFSM` to consume during recovery, but it does not. It buffers `applyCh`, not
`fsmMutateCh`, and the FSM goroutine is not started until after
`restoreFromCommittedLogs` returns.

## Finding 3: recovery moves the public commit index behind restored FSM state

Severity: low to medium; persistent state inconsistency visible through the
public API

Affected code:

- `api.go:598-607`: `restoreSnapshot` restores the FSM and sets `lastApplied` to
  the snapshot index.
- `api.go:746-753`: `restoreFromCommittedLogs` unconditionally replaces the
  commit index with the tracker's value.

Expected behavior: `commitIndex` is the highest log entry known to be committed,
while `lastApplied` is the highest entry applied to the FSM. The restored
snapshot necessarily represents committed state, so
`CommitIndex() >= AppliedIndex()` must hold.

Actual behavior: taking a snapshot does not append a log entry, so the last
durably staged commit can be one or more indices behind the snapshot. On a
restart, snapshot restore sets `lastApplied` to the snapshot index 3, then
committed-log recovery sets `commitIndex` to the stale tracker value 2.
`Raft.CommitIndex()` consequently reports 2 while `Raft.AppliedIndex()` reports
3. The code does not raise the recovered value to `lastApplied`.

This is a local state-invariant/API defect. A later leader heartbeat can repair
the in-memory value, but until then commit status is false and monitoring or
logic based on the public index sees impossible state.

Reproduction:
`TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsDoesNotRegressCommitBehindSnapshot` in
`audit_repro_test.go`.

Command:

```text
go test -run '^TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsDoesNotRegressCommitBehindSnapshot$' -count=1 -v .
```

Observed result:

```text
restored from snapshot: id=2-3-... last-index=3 ...
skipping application of old log: index=2
audit_repro_test.go:156: commit index regressed behind restored state: commit=2 applied=3
--- FAIL: TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsDoesNotRegressCommitBehindSnapshot (0.38s)
```

Alternative considered: a low recovered commit index might merely reduce the
optimization benefit if it were only internal. That does not explain the public
contradiction with `AppliedIndex`, and `CommitIndex` is documented as the highest
known committed entry. Recovery should use at least `max(trackerIndex,
lastApplied)`.

## Combined reproduction

Command:

```text
go test -run '^TestAudit' -count=1 -v .
```

Observed result:

```text
--- FAIL: TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsRestoresConfiguration (0.33s)
--- FAIL: TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsDoesNotDeadlockBeforeRunFSM (2.00s)
--- FAIL: TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsDoesNotRegressCommitBehindSnapshot (0.38s)
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/hashicorp/raft	2.742s
```

No captured source or dependency files were modified. The regression tests are
isolated in `work/audit_repro_test.go`.

The full suite was also run in the isolated local-network runner with
`go test ./...`. All pre-existing tests passed; the only suite failures were
the two audit tests above. The complete runner log is execution
`bfb4339e0c6943ceb1a8c40de3a77dc8`.

## Unresolved work

- Probe snapshot/configuration boundary cases and stale commit indices.
- Examine whether the in-memory commit-tracking store violates its own
  atomicity contract in useful crash simulations.

    25		})

    29		if err := leader.Apply([]byte("one"), time.Second).Error(); err != nil {

    37		cfg := leader.config()

    39		if err != nil {

    41		}

    44		configurationFuture := restarted.GetConfiguration()
    45		if err := configurationFuture.Error(); err != nil {
    46			t.Fatalf("get configuration after recovery: %v", err)
    47		}
    48		got := configurationFuture.Configuration().Servers
    49		if len(got) != 1 || got[0].ID != leader.localID {
    50			t.Fatalf("configuration after recovery = %+v, want local server %q", got, leader.localID)
    51		}

    57	func TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsDoesNotDeadlockBeforeRunFSM(t *testing.T) {

    79			t.Fatalf("bootstrap: %v", err)
    80		}
    81		for index := uint64(2); index <= entries; index++ {
    82			// Stage the preceding prefix with the final log-store call, matching
    83			// CommitTrackingLogStore's contract that staging will be persisted
    84			// atomically with a following StoreLogs call.

# HashiCorp Raft correctness audit

Source identity: `0f543c056e7e577a54b819a62116335c9661a13a`

The implementation's new `RestoreCommittedLogs` startup mode has three
independently reproducible correctness defects. All occur with supported
configuration values and do not require a cluster-wide fault.

## Finding 1: committed-log recovery discards the persisted cluster configuration

Severity: high

Affected code:

- `api.go:607-625`: `NewRaft` invokes `restoreFromCommittedLogs`, then starts its
  configuration scan at `max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1`.
- `api.go:720-755`: `restoreFromCommittedLogs` sets `lastApplied` to the persisted
  commit index via `processLogs`.
- `raft.go:1296-1363`: `processLogs` applies entries to the FSM, but never calls
  `processConfigurationLogEntry` or updates `r.configurations`.

Expected behavior: enabling `RestoreCommittedLogs` should replay the committed
log suffix to the FSM without losing Raft's own persistent state. In particular,
after restart, the latest committed configuration must be reconstructed from
configuration entries in that suffix. This is the behavior of the same startup
path with `RestoreCommittedLogs` disabled, and is required before the node can
evaluate elections or membership safely.

Actual behavior: on startup, `processLogs` advances `lastApplied` through the
persisted commit index. The subsequent configuration scan deliberately starts
after `lastApplied`, so it skips every configuration entry in the replayed
range. No other recovery step populates `r.configurations`. A restarted node can
therefore have an empty or stale `latest` configuration even though its log
contains the committed current configuration.

This occurs without a snapshot. With one bootstrapped voter and one committed
client command, the persisted tracker reaches the committed no-op and command.
After restart, the log still contains the bootstrap configuration at index 1,
but `restarted.GetConfiguration()` returns an empty configuration and the node
logs `initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]`.

Reproduction: `TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsRestoresConfiguration` in
`audit_repro_test.go`.

Command:

```text
go test -run '^TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsRestoresConfiguration$' -count=1 -v .
```

Observed result:

```text
server-...: initial configuration: index=1 servers="[{Suffrage:Voter ID:server-... Address:...}]"
server-...: initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]
audit_repro_test.go:64: configuration after recovery = [], want local server "server-..."
--- FAIL: TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsRestoresConfiguration (0.33s)
```

The first `initial configuration` line is the original startup. The second is
the recovery-enabled restart immediately after `NewRaft` returns.
Running this test ten times produced ten failures, so the observation is not a
startup race.

The same defect occurs with a snapshot containing an older configuration. A
separate reproducer installs a valid snapshot at index 1 with the old
configuration, stores a committed configuration change at index 2, and restarts.
Recovery keeps the old configuration from the snapshot instead of installing
the newer committed configuration. This is
`TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsAppliesConfigurationAfterSnapshot` in
`audit_repro_test.go`; its observed result is:

```text
initial configuration: index=1 servers="[{...}]"
audit_repro_test.go:237: configuration after recovery = {Servers:[one server]}, want {Servers:[two servers]}
--- FAIL: TestAuditRestoreCommittedLogsAppliesConfigurationAfterSnapshot (0.00s)
```

Alternative considered: perhaps the FSM-side configuration application is
intended to replace the Raft configuration scan. It cannot: `processLogs` only
queues `commitTuple`s for `runFSM`; `runFSM` may call an application
`ConfigurationStore`, but never mutates `Raft.configurations`, which is used by
elections, quorum calculation, and `GetConfiguration`.

Audit completed. The report is at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_09-39-48-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md), with reproducible tests in [audit_repro_test.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_09-39-48-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/audit_repro_test.go).

Three concrete defects were confirmed:

- `RestoreCommittedLogs` loses current cluster configuration because recovery advances `lastApplied` before the configuration scan.
- Startup deadlocks after 129 FSM batches because recovery writes to `fsmMutateCh` before `runFSM` starts.
- A snapshot newer than the persisted commit tracker causes `CommitIndex()` to regress below `AppliedIndex()`.

All findings have deterministic failing tests. The isolated full suite passed every pre-existing test; the four audit test functions were the only failures. Complete output is retained under execution `d6e2274cbc9c45c3bbbffbdcf43b2e0b`. No captured implementation or dependency files were changed.
